name: Sketch To Animation Ladder
use_when: A scripted beat needs a diagram, flowchart, process animation, or visual explanation.
The editor must decide whether a simple design tool is enough or whether After Effects/Remotion is justified.
A complex animation risks being built before the idea is clear.
avoid_when: A real clip, screenshot, or simple text card communicates the beat faster.
The animation would consume more time than the line's importance justifies.
The user needs editable native NLE graphics only.

timeline_pattern.pattern: spoken_concept -> paper_sketch -> simple_or_advanced_tool_choice -> build_base_shapes_text_paths -> sync_to_voiceover -> add_motion_glow_texture -> export_or_render -> timeline_align
timeline_pattern.sketch_rule: Sketch the animation before opening the motion tool so the agent knows the boxes, arrows, text, reveal order, and focus path.
timeline_pattern.tool_ladder_rule: Use a simple tool for simple text/shape animations; use After Effects or Remotion when path motion, detailed reveals, or reusable animation systems are needed.
timeline_pattern.resolution_rule: Export simple-tool animations at higher resolution when the edit will zoom into them later.

motion.rule: Build the base design first, then animate reveals, zooms, typewriter text, Trim Paths, and glow in sync with the voiceover.

sound.rule: Add SFX after the animation timing is known; do not let whooshes distract from the diagram's explanation.

captions.rule: Suppress captions if the animation text already carries the spoken idea and screen space is limited.

color.rule: Use the same palette and contrast rules as the rest of the video so the animation feels native.

implementation.ffmpeg: Composite exported animation renders over the timeline and use scale/crop tests to verify zoom readability.
implementation.remotion: Create a data-driven diagram component with nodes, arrows, revealOrder, focusZoomFrames, textBlurState, and captionSuppression.
implementation.blender: Use curves, text objects, and camera moves for spatial diagrams only when 3D depth helps understanding.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Build simple boxes/text/arrows in a design tool, export high resolution, then add keyframed zooms and captions in the edit app.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use simple graphics for low-complexity beats; send advanced sketches to After Effects for text, shape, pen, typewriter, Trim Paths, glow, and easing.

common_mistakes: Opening After Effects with no sketch and inventing the animation while keyframing.
Using an advanced animation tool for a beat that needed only a clean text card.
Exporting a simple animation too low-resolution and then zooming into a soft render.
Letting the animation reveal order lag behind the voiceover.
qc: Is there a sketch or written plan before animation begins?
Is the chosen tool complexity justified by the line's importance?
Does the reveal order match the voiceover?
Is the exported animation sharp after any timeline zoom?
Does the animation explain the concept faster than extra narration would?
